headline.en: Subject-Verb Concord — Matching Subject with Verb
headline.hi: Subject-Verb Concord — Subject ko Verb se Match Karna

subtext.en: Singular Subject → Singular Verb | Plural Subject → Plural Verb
subtext.hi: Singular Subject → Singular Verb | Plural Subject → Plural Verb

text.en: Learn the Detective Method to spot the real subject in any sentence — most SVA mistakes disappear instantly.
text.hi: Detective Method seekho aur kisi bhi sentence ka real subject pehchano — zyadatar SVA mistakes turant khatam ho jayengi.

content.en:
Basic Rule (Sabse Important)

Singular Subject → Singular Verb (s/es lagta hai)
• She reads books.
• He plays cricket.
• The boy runs fast.

Plural Subject → Plural Verb (s/es NAHI lagta)
• They read books.
• We play cricket.
• The boys run fast.

Simple Trick: Subject ke saath verb ka form match karo. Singular = s/es wala verb | Plural = bina s/es wala verb

content.en:
🕵️ Play Detective — Find the REAL Subject First

90% of Subject-Verb Concord mistakes happen because students match the verb to the WRONG word — usually a word sitting right next to the verb that isn't actually the subject.

The Detective Method — 3 steps before you write the verb:
1. Cross out every phrase starting with of, with, along with, as well as, in addition to, together with — these are distractions, never the real subject.
2. Find the word that's left — THAT is your real subject.
3. Match the verb to THAT word, ignoring everything you crossed out.

Example: "The box of chocolates ~~of chocolates~~ is on the table." (Real subject = box, singular → is, NOT 'are' even though 'chocolates' is plural and sits right before the verb)

This one habit alone fixes most SVA errors instantly — in gap-filling AND editing questions.
content.hi:
🕵️ Detective Bano — Pehle REAL Subject Dhundo

90% Subject-Verb Concord mistakes isliye hoti hain kyunki students verb ko GALAT word se match kar dete hain — usually woh word jo verb ke bilkul paas baitha hai but real subject nahi hai.

Detective Method — verb likhne se pehle 3 steps:
1. Har phrase cross out karo jo of, with, along with, as well as, in addition to, together with se start hota hai — ye distractions hain, kabhi real subject nahi.
2. Jo word bacha hai wo dhundo — WAHI tumhara real subject hai.
3. Verb ko USI word se match karo, jo cross out kiya usse ignore karo.

Example: "The box of chocolates ~~of chocolates~~ is on the table." (Real subject = box, singular → is, 'are' NAHI chahe 'chocolates' plural ho aur verb ke bilkul pehle baitha ho)

Sirf ye ek habit follow karne se zyadatar SVA errors turant fix ho jaate hain — gap-filling AUR editing dono mein.

content.en:
Rule 1: 'And' ke saath Plural Verb

Jab do subjects 'and' se jude hain → hamesha PLURAL verb

• Ram and Shyam are playing. (do subjects = plural)
• The teacher and the student were talking.

Exception: 'Bread and butter', 'Rice and curry' jaise fixed phrases singular treat hote hain.
• Bread and butter is my favourite breakfast. (singular)
content.hi:
Rule 1: 'And' ke saath Plural Verb

Jab do subjects 'and' se jude hain → hamesha PLURAL verb

• Ram and Shyam are playing. (do subjects = plural)
• The teacher and the student were talking.

Exception: 'Bread and butter', 'Rice and curry' jaise fixed phrases singular treat hote hain.
• Bread and butter is my favourite breakfast. (singular)

content.en:
Rule 2: 'Or', 'Either...or', 'Neither...nor'

Jab 'or', 'either...or', 'neither...nor' se subjects jude hain → verb SECOND subject ke hisaab se aata hai.

• Either Ram or his friends are coming. (friends = plural → plural verb)
• Neither the students nor the teacher was present. (teacher = singular → singular verb)

Memory Trick: 'Or' waale mein jo subject PAAS mein hai (second wala), uske hisaab se verb banao.
content.hi:

Memory Trick: 'Or' waale mein jo subject PAAS mein hai (second wala), uske hisaab se verb banao.

content.en:
Rule 3: Collective Nouns (Team, Class, Family)

Collective nouns (team, class, family, committee, crowd) usually take SINGULAR verb jab group ek unit ki tarah kaam kare.

• The team is playing well. (ek unit ki tarah)
• The family has decided to move.

Exception: Jab group ke members individually dikhaye jayein → PLURAL verb
• The team are arguing among themselves. (alag-alag members ki baat)

Exception: Jab group ke members individually dikhaye jayein → PLURAL verb

content.en:
Rule 4: 'Each', 'Every', 'Either', 'Neither' → Singular

'Each', 'Every', 'Either', 'Neither', 'One', 'No one' ke baad hamesha SINGULAR verb aata hai.

• Each student has submitted the project.
• Every boy was present in class.
• Neither of them is coming.
• One of my friends lives in Delhi.

Memory Trick: 'Each' aur 'Every' ka matlab hi 'ek-ek' hota hai → singular.

content.en:
Rule 5: 'The number of' vs 'A number of'

'The number of' = Singular (number ki baat ho rahi hai)
• The number of students is increasing.

'A number of' = Plural (bahut saare ki baat ho rahi hai)
• A number of students are absent today.

Memory Trick:
• THE number = woh EK number → singular
• A number = kuch log (bahut saare) → plural

Memory Trick:
• THE number = woh EK number → singular
• A number = kuch log (bahut saare) → plural

content.en:
Rule 6: Uncountable Nouns → Singular Verb

Uncountable nouns (water, sugar, advice, news, furniture, information) hamesha SINGULAR verb lete hain.

• The news is shocking. (NOT 'are shocking')
• This furniture is expensive.
• Her advice was very helpful.

Memory Trick: Uncountable = gin nahi sakte → ek hi treat karo → singular verb

content.en:
Rule 7: Distance/Time/Amount → Singular

Jab distance, time, ya amount subject ban jaayein → hamesha SINGULAR verb.

• Ten miles is too far to walk.
• Five thousand rupees was stolen.
• Two hours is enough for this test.

Memory Trick: Distance/time/amount ko ek unit ki tarah treat karo → singular verb

content.en:
🥊 Confusion Buster — 'Each/Every' vs the Noun That Follows

Students see a PLURAL-looking noun after 'each'/'every' and instinctively reach for a plural verb. Wrong reflex.

Rule that never breaks: Each/Every + [any noun, even if it looks plural] → verb is ALWAYS singular.

• "Each of the students has submitted the assignment." (students is plural, but 'has' is correct — because it's EACH one, one at a time)
• "Every boy and girl was given a certificate." (even with 'and' — 'every' overrides the usual 'and = plural' rule)

Why: 'Each' and 'Every' mean 'one at a time' — so no matter how many nouns follow, grammatically you're always talking about ONE at a time → singular verb, always.
content.hi:
🥊 Confusion Buster — 'Each/Every' vs Uske Baad Wala Noun

Students 'each'/'every' ke baad PLURAL-dikhne wala noun dekh kar instinctively plural verb use kar dete hain. Ye galat reflex hai.

Ye rule kabhi nahi tootta: Each/Every + [koi bhi noun, plural dikhe bhi toh] → verb HAMESHA singular hoga.

• "Each of the students has submitted the assignment." (students plural hai, but 'has' hi sahi hai — kyunki EACH ek-ek karke ki baat hai)
• "Every boy and girl was given a certificate." (even 'and' ke saath bhi — 'every' usual 'and = plural' rule ko override kar deta hai)

Kyun: 'Each' aur 'Every' ka matlab hai 'ek-ek karke' — isliye kitne bhi nouns baad mein aayein, grammatically tum hamesha ek ki baat kar rahe ho → singular verb, hamesha.
